title: Record the vacuous-uniformity evidence trap in the repository profile
description:
Continuous-improvement capture from the QCLI-339 / QCLI-340 exchange with opum-agent on 2026-09-18. Two sessions made the same evidence error within an hour, in two repositories, on two different languages tooling, and neither caught it themselves.

The error: reading an ABSENT key as a null VALUE and resting a conclusion on it. jq renders a missing key as null; Python .get() renders it as None. Both look like a measured value.

Why it is worth a profile section rather than only a task note: the null was not weak evidence, it was ZERO evidence, and it read as STRONG evidence precisely because it was perfectly uniform across every record. Uniformity is the signature of a field that does not exist, and it is exactly what a clean measurement feels like. The lesson currently lives on the QCLI-339 record, which is a completed task nobody will read; the profile is loaded every session.

This is adjacent to but distinct from the existing name-the-object-you-measured and claim-that-was-true-when-written sections. Those are about measuring the wrong object, or a right measurement going stale. This is about a measurement that never had an object at all.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The repository profile in CLAUDE.md carries the rule, stating the uniformity signature rather than only the incident, with the check to run (test key presence, or grep the producing source for the field name) before resting anything on a null
Both measurements are cited with their repositories and attributed, and opum-agents half is marked as theirs
The section states what it does NOT duplicate, so it is not read as a restatement of the two adjacent sections
The edit is confined to the repository profile and changes no managed block or generated bytes

implementationNotes: CONFINEMENT VERIFIED MECHANICALLY, not by eye (criterion 4). git diff --stat reports 53 insertions and ZERO deletions on CLAUDE.md, so no existing line was touched. quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude exits 0 with state version-only and skill state current, meaning the managed block content is byte-identical and only the pinned version number differs -- the documented non-failing state, unrelated to this edit. lore check exits 0, 63 files, 0 errors.

WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE SECTION RATHER THAN A LINE ON AN EXISTING ONE (criterion 3). Three failure shapes look alike from a distance and the profile now says which gap each covers: name-the-object-you-measured is measuring the WRONG object; a-claim-that-was-true-when-written is a RIGHT measurement going stale; this one is a measurement that never had an object at all. The distinguishing property, and the reason it deserves its own entry, is that it gets MORE convincing the more thoroughly you check, which is the opposite of how the other two fail.
finalSummary:
Added a repository-profile section recording the vacuous-uniformity evidence trap, so the correction leaves an artifact where it will actually be read rather than only on a completed task record.

WHAT IT RECORDS. Reading an ABSENT key as a null VALUE and resting a conclusion on it. jq renders a missing key as null; Python .get() renders it as None; both are indistinguishable from a measured value. The rule kept is opum-agents framing rather than my first one: the null was not weak evidence, it was ZERO evidence, and it read as STRONG evidence precisely because it was perfectly uniform. Uniformity across every member of a population is what a clean measurement feels like AND what a nonexistent field produces. The section gives the checks (test key presence with has(), grep the producing source for the field name) and says to prefer provenance to absence where a record of origin exists.

BOTH MEASUREMENTS CITED AND ATTRIBUTED. Mine in quest-cli: QCLI-339 and PR #190 cited no-history and completedAt-null to identify 201 records as Backlog imports; grep -rn completedAt src/ returns nothing and neither field exists. Theirs in opum-agent, marked as theirs: they made the same error and escalated it into a causal hypothesis, then re-tested by key presence and found "completedAt" in record true for 0 of 226 records.

TWO SECOND-ORDER POINTS KEPT because they generalise past this instance. A false cause dressed in a known-true pattern is harder to dislodge than a bare wrong number -- the held-version-naming-two-byte-sets pattern is real and documented in the shared block, which is exactly why invoking it was persuasive. And the mirror-image failure from the same hour is recorded beside it: on QCLI-340 the orchestrators reasoning had a wrong BASIS and a surviving CONCLUSION, since the population it called empty was not, so taking it at face value would have shipped the right fix for a reason that would not hold next time.

WHY A SEPARATE SECTION. Three failure shapes look alike from a distance, and the section states which gap each covers so it is not read as a restatement: wrong object, stale measurement, and no object at all. The distinguishing property is that this one gets MORE convincing the more thoroughly you check.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED. Confinement asserted mechanically rather than by eye: git diff --stat shows 53 insertions and ZERO deletions on CLAUDE.md, so no existing line was touched. quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude exits 0 at state version-only with skill state current, so the managed block content is byte-identical. lore check exits 0 across 63 files. No source or test files are in the diff.
